findings.title: scripts_refreshed[] gains three required fields with no schema_version gate, breaking any round already recorded under the old 2-field contract
locations: src/CLI/Rounds.jl :: refresh_scripts (base entry construction, now replaced)
src/CLI/RoundFiles.jl:86-98 :: rounds() (swallows a schema failure into state = :invalid)
src/CLI/Doctor.jl :: ROUND.MARKER, ROUND.FROZEN, ROUND.DEV, AUDIT.GAP (all filter RoundFiles.rounds() by state)
src/TestHarness.jl:604-611 :: gate() (hard error()s on a nonzero QUICK doctor code)
test/runtests.jl:28 (unconditionally calls TestHarness.gate(; root = TOOL) against the tool's own real .gbg/)
findings.before: schema/round.schema.json: scripts_refreshed[].required = ["at", "head"], additionalProperties: false; and the base refresh_scripts wrote `entry = Dict{String,Any}("at" => timestamp(), "head" => something(Git.head(cfg["root"]), "0"^40))` -- exactly two fields, no `--reason` flag existed yet to supply a third.
findings.after: schema/round.schema.json: scripts_refreshed[].required = ["at", "head", "reason", "after_pass", "scripts"], additionalProperties still false, so an entry with only `at`/`head` no longer validates.
findings.why_it_matters: load_schema() always reads the CURRENT schema/round.schema.json from the running copy -- it has no notion of the schema_version a given ROUND.toml was written under -- so a round anywhere (this repository's own history, or a consumer's, once it adopts this version) that ever ran the pre-existing `gbg round scripts <round>` verb has a scripts_refreshed entry with only {at, head} and will now fail RoundFiles.read_round's schema check. RoundFiles.rounds() catches that failure generically and reclassifies the round's state as :invalid rather than :closed/:open/:abandoned. Every downstream reader that filters on state then behaves differently for exactly the same on-disk file than it did before this diff: ROUND.MARKER (in the QUICK doctor set) newly FAILs with an opaque 'round directories without a valid ROUND.toml' instead of passing, while ROUND.FROZEN, ROUND.DEV, AUDIT.GAP and Release.cites_round silently stop seeing that round at all (no warning, it simply drops out of their coverage). Because test/runtests.jl calls TestHarness.gate(), which error()s the whole test run when doctor(cfg, :QUICK) is non-zero, this specific FAIL is capable of failing Pkg.test() itself on any repository -- including the tool's own, self-application being mandatory under D15 -- if a historical round with an old-shape entry is present. The diff's own comments name a concrete precedent for exactly this shape of incident (2026-09-12-check-docs-01, scripts refreshed 'by hand') but the diffstat carries no change under .gbg/rounds/, so no existing record was migrated to the new required shape.
findings.description: The new required fields (reason, after_pass, scripts) are a real improvement -- they make a rare, exceptional, mid-round operation auditable -- but the change tightens an already-shipped artefact schema with no version selection and no migration of already-persisted records, and no test constructs an old-shape entry to check it still reads. This is precisely the shape the round's own design elsewhere calls out as unacceptable when it happens to a measurement ('a skipped class is UNDEFINED in recall, so the denominator shrinks in silence') -- except here what shrinks in silence is the doctor's and the release gate's own historical coverage of past rounds.
findings.evidence:
diff hunk in schema/round.schema.json: `-     "at",
-     "head"
+     "at",
+     "head",
+     "reason",
+     "after_pass",
+     "scripts"` under `"additionalProperties": false`; base src/CLI/Rounds.jl: `entry = Dict{String,Any}("at" => timestamp(), "head" => something(Git.head(cfg["root"]), "0"^40))`.

findings.title: A policy waiver on a scan's non-canonical rule, previously honored (if over-broadly), now throws an uncaught LedgerError instead of failing gracefully
locations: src/CLI/Main.jl :: main() (only Config.ConfigError is caught as exit 2; every other exception is exit 3 with a backtrace)
findings.before: "An entry `scope = \"policy\"` with target `*` on ANY rule the scan enforces ... disables the scan (every hit exempted, `disabled = true`) ... The mirror case is NOT fixed and is a known limit: a waiver on either rule still disables the WHOLE scan, so it withdraws enforcement of a sibling rule the consumer never exempted." -- i.e. at base, a policy-scope waiver recorded against either of a two-rule scan's rules was silently ACCEPTED and ran (over-broadly disabling the scan).
findings.after: `for rule in rules_for_scan(id); rule == canonical && continue; e = first(Ledger.entries(ledger, rule; scope = "policy"), 1); isempty(e) || throw(Ledger.LedgerError("$rule on $(e[1][\"target\"]) is a policy waiver of a rule $id enforces but does not own ..."))` -- the same ledger entry now raises, and CFG.EXEMPTIONS separately reports it as FAIL.
findings.why_it_matters: A `.gbg/exemptions.toml` entry recorded under the OLD contract against RULE.CIT.DOI, RULE.CIT.NO_INACCESSIBLE, or RULE.DOC.API_GROUPING (the non-canonical rule of SCAN.DOI_CROSSCHECK / SCAN.DEAD_REF / SCAN.API_PAGE_STRUCTURE respectively) -- previously valid input that ran without error, and that `gbg sync` may already have rendered into deviations.md as a granted deviation -- now makes `gbg scan docs`, `gate()`, or any check-docs/check-consistency round over that ledger raise Ledger.LedgerError. Because main()'s exception handling special-cases only Config.ConfigError, this is not the documented exit-2 'cannot evaluate' path but an exit-3 crash with a full backtrace, for a file the consumer owns and previously wrote correctly by the tool's own former contract.
findings.description: The underlying defect is real and was explicitly flagged as an open 'known limit' in the docstring this diff replaces, and the fix is well tested (test/scans.jl rewrites the whole scenario across all three two-rule scans, and test/sync_doctor.jl adds a doctor-level check). But the transition is abrupt: there is no deprecation warning, no grace period, and the failure mode for previously-accepted input is a hard crash rather than a graceful diagnostic, because the pre-existing LedgerError path was never wired into the same exit-2 treatment Config.ConfigError just received in this same diff.
findings.evidence: diff hunk in src/Scan.jl apply_ledger: removed `enforced = unique!(vcat(String(row["rule"]), rules_for_scan(id))); for rule in enforced, e in Ledger.entries(ledger, rule; scope = "policy")` (waived any enforced rule); added the canonical-only loop plus the throw quoted above.

findings.title: latex_source_globs changes from replace-when-set to always-union-with-the-four-defaults, removing any way to narrow the panel's source surface
locations: instruments/check-consistency/workflow/verify-state.js (SCOPE now always CLI-resolved, the ['src','ext','docs/src','docs'] literal fallback removed)
findings.before: "instruments.check-consistency.latex_source_globs, resolved by preflight: the AUTHORED SOURCE ... the consumer's globs when it set any, the four default surfaces otherwise." and `globs = String.(get(...)); a["source_globs"] = isempty(globs) ? ["src", "ext", "docs/src", "docs"] : globs` -- a consumer that sets the key gets ONLY its own globs.
findings.after: "the four default surfaces (src, ext, docs/src, docs) followed by every glob the consumer names -- added to them, never in place of them." and `source_globs(cfg) = unique!(vcat(SOURCE_SURFACES, String.(get(...))))` -- a consumer that sets the key now always gets the four defaults too.
findings.why_it_matters: Any consumer config that already sets instruments.check-consistency.latex_source_globs -- to point the panel's source-needing hats and the pass's state verifier at a narrower or different surface than src/ext/docs/src/docs -- gets a different resolved source_globs after this diff purely from the tool version bump, with no change to its own config. There is now no way to exclude the four standard surfaces from a 'needs: source' hat's reading list.
findings.description: This looks like the correct fix and is thoroughly documented, schema-described, and tested (test/coverage.jl asserts both the unset and set cases, and checks the state verifier's own literal fallback was removed). It reverses a genuine regression from the immediately preceding round (2026-09-12-audit-changes-02, which itself had turned a no-reader bug into a replace-semantics bug). Flagged here only because it is a second, real change in what this key resolves to for identical config input within two rounds, and the 'replace' capability is removed outright rather than kept as an opt-in.
findings.evidence: instruments/check-consistency/schema.json diff: '- ... the consumer's globs when it set any, the four default surfaces otherwise.' -> '+ ... the four default surfaces (src, ext, docs/src, docs) followed by every glob the consumer names — added to them, never in place of them.'
